newsitem.title: USA: Broadcasters, DB satellite firms nearing pact - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Broadcasters, DB satellite firms nearing pact - WSJ.

text.p: Television broadcasters and three direct-broadcast satellite companies have tentatively agreed to end a fight over certain customers who illegally receive network programs, the Wall Street Journal said in its electronic edition Tuesday.
The pact covers only customers receiving signals from distant cities and would cancel access to these signals within a year for thousands of customers receiving them illegally, the report said.

Direct broadcast satellite firms don't offer local network broadcast signals, as cable does, and viewers getting signals from distant cities are not counted in local audiences, thereby cutting advertising revenues, the report said.
It said the pact involves the National Association of Broadcasters, Tele-Communications' Netlink, PrimeStar Partners and EchoStar Communications Corp.
